info.title: Tier0 Cloud OpenAPI v2
info.description:
Cloud collections, records, samples, sources, streams and App policy management. Use an API key bound to a workspace.

### UNS API errors

For `/uns/` operations, see the `default` response for the error schema. Use `error.code` to identify the specific cause.

| HTTP status | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `401` | Authentication is missing or invalid. |
| `403` | Access is denied or the feature is disabled. |
| `404` | The resource was not found. |
| `409` | Conflict involving state, revision, a uniqueness constraint, or credentials. |
| `413` | The request content is too large. |
| `422` | Input or business rule validation failed. |
| `429` | The service is overloaded. |
| `500` | The server encountered an error. |
| `503` | The service is unavailable. |
| `504` | The query timed out. |

| `error.execution` | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `notStarted` | Execution did not start. No changes were committed. |
| `rolledBack` | Execution was rolled back. No changes were committed. |
| `committed` | Changes were committed. For a batch, check which items succeeded. |
| `unknown` | The server cannot confirm whether the write was committed. This status only applies to writes. |

| Retry signal | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| `error.retry.safe: true` | Resend the same request. For writes, reuse the original idempotency key if you supplied one. |
| `error.retry.safe: false` | Address the cause before trying again. For example, correct the request or restore access. |
| `error.retry.afterMs` or `Retry-After` | Wait at least the indicated time before retrying. |

### Platform APIs

Platform operations use the response format documented for each endpoint.

| Endpoint | Response format |
| --- | --- |
| File download | HTTP `302` redirect. |
| Notifications, capability discovery, Stream requests, and message connections | JSON payload returned directly. |
| Other platform operations | JSON envelope with `code`, `msg`, and `data`. |

post.description: Query resource references by targets. Collection App references include grants and policy status for that Collection. Stream references include only frozen dependencies of the currently effective release: relationship.access describes read/write access to this target, and data.sourceIds contains the unique, sorted Source IDs bound by the same release. With Source read permission, no bindings returns an empty array. Without that permission, the field is omitted while the Stream reference remains visible. An omitted field does not mean no bindings. Drafts, historical releases and disabled Streams are excluded. Version selection is not supported. Use kinds to select app/stream/source/topic. status=active excludes disabled configuration; filtering precedes permission checks and pagination. Dependencies do not prove active writes or per-record provenance. Each target is paginated independently and sorted by kind and ID. Continue using nextPage only for targets with hasMore. The total request row budget is 2000. With size=20, a batch can contain at most 100 targets. Hidden reference items continue to be indicated only by hasHiddenReferences.

get.description: GET; Accept must be exactly text/event-stream. collectionIds is a repeated query parameter, at most 64. Omission selects all readable collections for the identity, or all collections granted to the app. At most 100 recordIds are allowed and require exactly one collection. Each collection requires record:read. The connection immediately sends heartbeat with the current position as id, then every 15 seconds. change events arrive in commit order and contain only collectionId, recordId, revision, change (record/delete), restricted and occurredAt. Read business data again by ID. restricted=true indicates employee data rules; servers forwarding under app identity may forward only collection-level notifications to browsers. Reconnect with the last event id as Last-Event-ID. Exceeding 24-hour retention or narrowing authorization sends reset and closes the connection. Reread data and subscribe without Last-Event-ID. Authorization is rechecked every 30 seconds. Exceeding the connection limit returns 429 OVERLOADED.

With atomic=false, chunks/items commit independently. Once any commit occurs, failure reports error.execution=committed and retry.safe=false, with cumulative data matching the success structure: counts, insertedIds, writeErrors, hasMore and nextIndex, plus unknownUntil when outcomes are unknown. nextIndex is the first unexecuted zero-based operation; earlier indices absent from writeErrors committed. If unknownUntil is present, [nextIndex, unknownUntil) has unknown outcome. Retry with the same idempotency key if supplied. Without a key, only client-ID inserts and ID-based replacements/deletes can be reconciled by reading those IDs before continuation. Server-generated-ID inserts, filter-selected operations and incremental updates such as $inc cannot be reconciled safely; always use idempotency keys for these writes. Without unknownUntil, continuation from nextIndex is safe. execution is rolledBack or notStarted only when nothing committed.
